newsitem.title: FRANCE: Chirac urges French coalition to avoid squabbles.
newsitem.headline: Chirac urges French coalition to avoid squabbles.

text.p: French President Jacques Chirac appealed to his centre-right coalition on Wednesday to avoid feuding 12 days before a snap parliamentary election after criticism in his own ranks of Prime Minister Alain Juppe.

"Unfortunately, the serious debate worthy of our democracy, which is what interests the French people, is often masked by polemics and soundbites, from both the coalition and the opposition, which end up being the only things the public remembers," government spokesman Alain Lamassoure quoted Chirac as telling a weekly cabinet meeting.

Chirac did not refer directly to calls for Juppe's replacement and suggestions of alternative prime ministers from within the centre-right coalition, but he appeared to have that in mind in his comments to ministers.
"Don't respond to provocations and continue to avoid any polemics in setting out your proposals, your beliefs and your vision of the future," he was quoted as saying.

Ex-president Valery Giscard d'Estaing said last week the French people wanted to be "governed differently" and Urban Affairs Minister Eric Raoult said anti-Maastricht Gaullist National Assembly speaker Philippe Seguin, the favourite among right-wing voters accordint to polls, would make a good premier.
The Socialist and Communist opposition have made Juppe their chief target, causing discomfort on the right by telling voters they face "another five years of Juppe".
